slo_title: Implement insertion at the middle of singly linked lists

mcq.q: A student record management system stores student details using a singly linked list. A new student joins the class and needs to be inserted in alphabetical order in the middle of the list. What should be your first step

options.A: Add the student at the end of the list
options.B: Search for the correct position by comparing names one by one
options.C: Delete an existing student and replace them with the new one
options.D: Reverse the list and insert at the first position

mcq.answer_text: Search for the correct position by comparing names one by one

mcq.q: What does the following function do for a given Linked List with first node as head? void fun1(struct node* head) { if(head == NULL) return; fun1(head->next); printf("%d ", head->data); }

options.A: Prints all nodes of linked lists
options.B: Prints all nodes of linked list in reverse order
options.C: Prints alternate nodes of Linked List
options.D: Prints alternate nodes in reverse order

mcq.answer_text: Prints all nodes of linked list in reverse order

mcq.q: What happens when the last node is deleted from a singly linked list

options.B: The second-last node's next pointer is set to NULL
options.C: The entire linked list gets deleted

mcq.answer_text: The second-last node's next pointer is set to NULL
